content:
Apple today exclusively announced eight upcoming performances at the brand-new Apple Music Hall in London, with Elton John kicking things off next week. Here are the full details.

Elton John will headline the opening night of Apple Music Hall

Apple earlier this week unveiled Apple Music Hall — a new live music venue located at London's iconic Battersea Power Station, where Apple also has offices and a retail store.

Apple Music Hall can accommodate up to 600 guests, and performances will be live-streamed globally via Apple Music. Artists will also receive finished spatial audio recordings, broadcast-ready mixes, and multi-camera video footage.

When Apple first announced Apple Music Hall, the company said it would reveal the initial lineup of performers at the venue at a later date.

Apple today confirmed the lineup for the first eight shows, with Elton John kicking things off next week. Here's the full schedule:

  • Elton John — September 28
  • Baby Keem — October 2
  • Skye Newman — October 7
  • Troye Sivan — October 13
  • Arlo Parks — October 22
  • Burna Boy — October 29
  • Chase & Status — November 26
  • Charli xcx — December 2

Some of the artists have a longstanding connection with Apple Music. Elton John has hosted his weekly radio show "Rocket Hour" since Apple Music launched in 2015; Charli xcx previously hosted five seasons of her own show "The Candy Shop" on Beats 1.

On the concert front, Apple said tickets for Elton John, Baby Keem, and Skye Newman will go on sale Monday, September 28 at 9 a.m. UK time, while on-sale dates for all remaining shows will be announced later.

For more information about tickets and availability, click here.

Apple Music requires an active subscription. You can subscribe monthly for $11.99 with the first month free, or opt to bundle it with Apple One.
